subject: physics
title: The motor effect
key_idea: (Higher tier) A wire carrying a current in a magnetic field experiences a force, and the magnet experiences an equal and opposite force. Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of the force. For a wire at right angles to the field, F = B × I × l.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) A wire carrying a current in a magnetic field experiences a force. This is the motor effect.

items.meaning: The force on a conductor carrying a current in a magnetic field. The magnet and the conductor exert forces on each other.
The strength of the magnetic field. Its unit is the tesla (T).

items: The magnet's field and the field around the wire interact. This produces a force on the wire.
An equal and opposite force acts on the magnet.
Reverse the current or reverse the magnetic field to reverse the direction of the force.
To increase the force, increase the current or use a stronger magnet. A longer length of wire in the field also helps.
The motor effect is the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field.
The wire and the magnet exert equal and opposite forces on each other.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of the force. Use your left hand.

items.text: Hold the first finger, second finger and thumb at right angles to each other.
Point it in the direction of the magnetic field, north to south.
Point it in the direction of the current.
It points in the direction of the force, and so the motion.

items: First finger is the field, second finger is the current, thumb is the force.
The three must be at right angles to each other.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) For a conductor at right angles to the magnetic field, the force depends on the field, the current and the length in the field.

blocks.label: Force on a conductor
where: F is the force in newtons (N).
B is the magnetic flux density in tesla (T).
I is the current in amperes (A).
l is the length of conductor in the field in metres (m).

blocks.text: The equation is given on the equation sheet. You must convert units and rearrange it.

where: B is the magnetic flux density in tesla (T).

where: I is the current in amperes (A).

items.text: A wire of 50 mm carries 3.0 A in a field of 0.20 T. 50 mm = 0.050 m.

blocks.text: Change the field, current and length to see the force.

diagram.alt: Change the magnetic flux density, the current and the length of wire in the field to see the force.

inputs.label: Length of wire in the field

diagram.alt: Calculate the current in a wire from the force, the magnetic flux density and the length in the field.
diagram.question: A wire carries a current in a uniform magnetic field of flux density {B} T. The length of wire in the field is {L} mm. The force on the wire is {F} N. Calculate the current in the wire.

items: F = B × I × l, with the length in metres.
Convert mm to m, mA to A and mT to T before substituting.
Give the unit: N for force, T for flux density, A for current.

checks.q: Give two ways the direction of the force on a wire in a magnetic field could be reversed.
checks.a: Reverse the direction of the current. Reverse the direction of the magnetic field.

checks.q: A wire of length 0.075 m carries a current of 4.0 A at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.30 T. Calculate the force on the wire.
Describe how Fleming's left-hand rule can be used to find the direction of the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field.
checks.a: Hold the first finger, second finger and thumb of the left hand at right angles. The first finger is in the direction of the field and the second finger is in the direction of the current. The thumb shows the direction of the force.

mistakes.right: Convert the length first: 80 mm = 0.080 m. Then B = 0.092 ÷ (4.6 × 0.080) = 0.25 T.

mistakes.wrong: The reading on the balance increased because the wire got heavier.
mistakes.right: The downward force on the balance increased. The wire experiences an equal and opposite force, which is upwards.

worked_example.question:
The length of the wire in the magnetic field is 0.050 m.
The force on the wire is 0.072 N.
The magnetic flux density is 360 mT.

Calculate the current in the wire.
Use the Physics Equations Sheet.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the conversion, the substitution, the rearrangement and the answer. A correct answer of 4.0 A scores all 4 marks.

exam_phrases: first finger, second finger and thumb (of left-hand) held mutually perpendicular
first finger (is in the direction of) magnetic field
second finger (is in the direction of) current
thumb (is in the) direction of force / motion
magnetic fields interact
weight / gravitational force (downwards on upper magnet)
forces equal size / in equilibrium

mistakes.right: Convert 93.1 mA to 93.1 × 10⁻³ A. Then B = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ T. A power-of-ten error scores 1 mark only.

mistakes.wrong: Only an upward magnetic force acts on the floating magnet.
mistakes.right: The weight (gravitational force) also acts downwards. The forces are equal in size, so the magnet floats.

blocks.text: Magnetic flux density can also be given in newtons per ampere metre (N/A m). 1 T = 1 N/A m, so the equation is used in the same way.

worked_example.question:
A wire is in a uniform magnetic field.

The magnetic flux density of the magnetic field is 0.72 N/A m.
The length of the wire inside the field is 30 mm.
The size of the force due to the magnetic field on the wire is 0.045 N.

Calculate the size of the current in the wire.

Use an equation selected from the list of equations at the end of this paper.
answer_points: Substitution into F = B × I × l: 0.045 = 0.72 × I × 30 (× 10⁻³).
worked_example.tip: One mark each for substitution, rearrangement and evaluation. Rearrangement and substitution can be in either order.

exam_phrases: the magnet will exert a force on the wire
(current in the wire) creates a magnetic field
the magnetic fields of the magnet and wire interact
F = BIL
increase the current (in the coil)
increase the number of coils
increase the length of the coil (in the magnetic field)
increase the strength of the magnet / magnetic field

mistakes.wrong: Use a bigger magnet to increase the force on the coil.
mistakes.right: Increase the strength of the magnet or magnetic field. The size of the magnet is ignored.

mistakes.wrong: Add an iron core to the coil to increase the force.
mistakes.right: Increase the current, the number of coils, the length of coil in the field or the strength of the magnet. An iron core is ignored.
Give the answer to the number of significant figures asked for. To 2 significant figures F = 1.1 N.

worked_example.question:
A wire of length 0.25 m experiences a force of 0.15 N when a current of 5.0 A flows.

Calculate the magnetic flux density of the field.

Use an equation from the data sheet to help you.
answer_points: F = BIL, so B = F ÷ (I × L)
worked_example.tip: Check the answer line first: 0.12 T scores all 3 marks.
